note: Human-reviewed functional examples only. New ALREADY_PRESENT decisions require actual native implementation evidence, not matching names. The remaining inventory retains HOLD_REVIEW or HOLD_CONFLICT; this file is never installation authorization.

decisions.reason: Upstream offers dedicated native Windows pywinauto/UIA guidance; public Toolkit has UI/browser QA guidance but no confirmed identical native Windows desktop test workflow. Managed native Codex install must be tested separately.
decisions.benefit: Native WPF/WinForms/Qt UIA E2E without web-UI automation confusion.
decisions.test_case: Original ECC --skills windows-desktop-e2e --target codex plan + dry-run in disposable HOME; no live model.

decisions.reason: Compared pinned ECC source with Toolkit change-impact-analysis, qa_change_impact.py and code-review: direct/downstream consumers, API/data/schema, tests, documentation, release and unknown call graph were already covered. Toolkit feature-delivery now explicitly reconciles pre-change scope against actual diff and records MATCHED/CHANGED/NOT_VERIFIED, avoiding a duplicate controller. Path-heuristic analysis is never claimed as full dependency graph.
decisions.benefit: Existing feature-delivery controller gains the high-risk before/after diff-alignment step while the license-constrained QA impact skill stays byte-unchanged; a separate ECC skill would duplicate core behavior.
decisions.test_case: Synthetic cross-module API+schema migration: inventory callers/contracts/rollout before implementation, compare actual diff after, flag uncovered consumer and unexecuted rollback NOT_VERIFIED. Verify no forced report folder, host command or secondary controller.

decisions.reason: Original skill explicitly marked DEPRECATED v1 and introduces Claude Stop-hook behavior. Do not install. Separate #436 must review v2 opt-in.
decisions.benefit: None for new installations; superseded upstream.
decisions.test_case: Ensure v1 is not included in approved adoption list.

decisions.reason: Original ECC TDD workflow adds a useful explicit RED/GREEN evidence cycle but mandates universal 80% coverage, all test layers, automatic staged Git checkpoints and upstream package manager detection; those are not justified across all Toolkit user projects. The existing feature-delivery controller now supports optional test-first RED/GREEN/refactor with real evidence and risk-based coverage, preserving project/owner policies, without copying a 21-KB second controller.
decisions.benefit: Opt-in TDD test-first evidence within Toolkit's canonical feature delivery, without automatic CLI/commits or arbitrary global coverage threshold.
decisions.test_case: Synthetic authorized bug fix: before-code test fails on intended behavior, same test passes after minimal change; missing runner and malformed plan produce NOT_VERIFIED, not fabricated RED/GREEN; no automatic git commit, 80% mandate or remote package-manager installer.

decisions.reason: Both source skills directly prescribe endpoint design, request/response/error semantics, pagination, versioning and compatibility. Toolkit includes consumer-version and rollout constraints in its existing canonical skill. No extra copy justified.
decisions.benefit: No incremental core workflow; retain Toolkit api-design.
decisions.test_case: Compare API-version/error/pagination examples in both original skill sources; existing canonical Skill Manager handles the work.

decisions.reason: Both sources explicitly cover expand-contract schema changes, resumable batch backfills, rollback and compatibility checks. Toolkit already requires lock budgets, restartability and recovery, so copying the ECC guidance would duplicate functionality.
decisions.benefit: No unique migration controller; retain existing Toolkit migrations gate.
decisions.test_case: Use synthetic expand-backfill-contract scenarios including legacy readers and roll-forward recovery.

decisions.reason: Original ECC covers Playwright E2E reliability and fixtures, and Toolkit already prescribes stable selectors, E2E setup, traces/screenshots, critical user journeys and test evidence. Toolkit source is framework-agnostic, not a literal Playwright POM tutorial; specialized examples may still need separate review.
decisions.benefit: Existing Toolkit QA coverage; no wholesale skill duplication.
decisions.test_case: Synthetic flaky web E2E with selector, permission flow and trace; original ECC example remains reference-only.
